definitions.explanation: Completely forgetting something, or the state of having been forgotten. A literary and formal word that carries a heavier nuance than simply forgetting — it suggests something has faded entirely from memory.

examples.japanese: {過去|かこ}を{忘却|ぼうきゃく}する。
examples.english: To consign the past to oblivion.

examples.japanese: あの{事件|じけん}は{忘却|ぼうきゃく}の{彼方|かなた}にある。
examples.english: That incident has faded into the depths of oblivion.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}が{経|た}てば、{辛|つら}い{記憶|きおく}も{忘却|ぼうきゃく}されていくものだ。
examples.english: With the passage of time, even painful memories fade into oblivion.

notes:
A formal, literary word. Much weightier than {忘|わす}れる (to forget), which is the everyday term. {忘却|ぼうきゃく} implies complete erasure from memory.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {忘却|ぼうきゃく}の{彼方|かなた} — beyond the reach of memory; deep in oblivion
- {忘却|ぼうきゃく}{曲線|きょくせん} — forgetting curve (psychology term)
- {忘却|ぼうきゃく}する — to forget completely (する verb)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {忘|わす}れる — to forget (everyday, neutral)
- {失念|しつねん} — to slip one's mind (polite/humble, used in business)
- {健忘|けんぼう} — forgetfulness (medical/clinical term)
